The graph above shows the curve $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ and the line $y=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}.$

The **exact** value of the $x$-coordinate of the point $A$ is 
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
The $y$-values of both functions are the same at the intersection point. Equating the two equations gives:

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡x=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
x=arctan\,(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})=-\frac{\pi }{6}
$$

This value lies outside $\frac{3\pi }{2}<x<\frac{5\pi }{2}.$ To get a value that's inside the required domain, we add $2\pi $ to the principal value. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =x+2\pi  \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+2\pi  \\  & =\frac{11\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the $x$-coordinate of $A$ is $\frac{11\pi }{6}.$
